The August 2025 Vesuvius fire (Terzigno, 7–9 August 2025) burned 761 ha; 596 ha burned moderately or badly, and 180 ha of that is 23° or steeper, where rain washes soil downhill most easily.

Treat first: 24 squares of 250×250 m (111 ha) where at least half the ground is both badly burned and steep. Most of them (22) form one continuous block centred on 40.8180 N, 14.4545 E — the highest ranks sit near 40.8241 N, 14.4530 E. Treat next: 19 squares (40 ha). The first squares keep only about 43% of the green cover of unburned ground, so little holds the soil.

The priority order barely changes if you use a different steepness limit. Full results: alert_cells.geojson, severity_20m.tif, main_fire_perimeter.geojson. This is an early assessment; rainfall was not modelled, so it ranks priority, not risk.

Overall greenness on Vesuvius changed little: the typical summer value was 0.509 in 2022 and 0.525 in 2024, so 2024 was slightly greener. Still, over the 14,269 hectares compared, 1,348 hectares (9.4%) lost green cover — a drop of at least 0.1 on the greenness scale used here. The losses are scattered rather than one big scar; the five largest patches were 8.4 ha (40.80468, 14.40179), 6.6 ha (40.83326, 14.37567), 4.5 ha (40.79034, 14.48553), 4.1 ha (40.80301, 14.4969) and 3.5 ha (40.80540, 14.40756). Green cover can fall from drought, harvesting, fire or building — this comparison shows where it fell, not why. Full maps: data/cache/runs/cee3c032d1c6/ndvi_change_20m.tif and ndvi_drop_patches.geojson.
